Santa (Hidden) Claus

By: Johann Botha | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We go all the way to the North Pole to track down the person behind millions of break-ins every December

Summary:
a mock investigative into the workings of Santa Clause - involving the hawks, SARS and the public protector

Further information:
We start off with a few kids (hidden identity) lodging complaints that they've been ripped off by Santa. They claim that there is a contract between Santa and themselves, where they have to behave for twelve months in return for some amazing gifts. Yet, in spite of them keeping their end of the deal, Santa hasn't been delivering what they asked for. Our investigation takes us to the hawks, who tell us that they are investigating a series of claimed robberies committed by Santa ranging from stealing the christmas pudding to a wittness who says that he saw Santa wearing his dad's shoes. From the hawks we go to SARS who says they are investigating the tax implications of all the gifts that he smuggles cross-border every year in December. The story ends in the office of the Public Protector who, after investigating all the claims rules that Santa is innocent of robbery, that he should be exempt from import tax because of the happines that he brings, and that those kids who complained are probably lying and did not behave well for the entire year. Therefore it is in the public good that we have a santa and he does not have to "pay back the money"

Press Release:


Every year thousands of houses are broken into over the festive season, while the owners are at home. And yet nothing is stolen during these break-ins. We investigate

Script:


SANTA
Bongani LINK
December is normally holiday time, and every year we receive warnings from police about break-ins into people’s homes, whilst they are living it up empty houses while the owners are living it up in exotic locations. But what few people mention is the apparent increase in break-ins where the occupants are present.
V/o
Security cam footage show some very interesting similarities between these break-ins. Apart from the fact that they only happen when the target family is at home, it’s also always apparent that the burglar visits the kitchen first.
V/o
But perhaps the most striking similarity between cases is strange skid marks and fresh animal droppings left on the lawn... The Hawks have long investigated but as these incidents take place only over a small December window period, the culprit has continued to evade arrest.
Interview hawks
Cop: There has been a lot of investigations that we have been dealing with, and from our side we’ve been trying to deal with it by all means, to make sure that we get the the person behind these break-ins.
Bon: So, you’re convinced, that it’s the same person?
Cop: One person, due to the fact that he’s very bold - in the sense that he has to leave his business card, just to make sure that he sends out a message out there, the he’s the one who is responsible.
Bon: But how can one person break into thousands of homes on the same night?
Cop: Well, that is one of the things that is really boggling us. It’s possible that he might be working with other people, but, we are actually looking for the main person. And that is why we are actually trying with all means from our side to make sure that we get him as well.
Bon: What’s your message to this guy?
Cop: Be careful. We are watching you, and the net is closing on you. We will arrest you.
Bongani at car outside OR Tambo international
We started a little investigation of our own. All the information we have points to a certain Mr Claus, who, I’m told, lives on the other side of the planet – somewhere close to the North Pole
V/o
It’s a long flight - Joburg via Oslo to Hammerfest, the northernmost town in the world. Braving minus 30 degrees temperatures in a place that won’t see the sun rise for another two months, I meet our informant at the local pub.
INTERVIEW
Bongani: How do you mean he's here, but he's not here?
Informant: Well he is here for 11 months of the year, but never in December. He packs up, he goes and we don’t know where he is going..
Bon: Can you take me to him? Can you show me where he lives?
informant: No, you must be crazy. It’s 20 degrees minus outside. And it’s dark, i’m not going outside.No-one knows where he is going or what he is doing, he is very secretive – which is all the more reason why we are so suspicious.
Bongani: Can you show me where he lives?
Informant: Are you crazy? It's freezing outside and it's dark – remember the sun doesn't rise here for three months this time of year...

We decide to go on our own - to Snøhvit or Snow White, on tiny Melkøya Island just off the coast of Hammerfest. Snøhvit is ostensibly a liquefied gas project run by the state, but our sources reveal the facility boasts a mammoth toy factory. As expected, it is closed over December - so we head back to South Africa where a new tip off leads to a small holding on the outskirts of Johannesburg.
Bongani Stables
Sources close to our investigation have told us these are the stables Santa uses for his reindeer when he’s in the country. We’ve spoken to the owner, who doesn’t want to give an on-camera interview, but confirms, that this is the right location. But, unfortunately for us, we’ve just missed him, he left about an hour ago.

Our next lead took me deeper - into the heart of Joburg - where one of my regular informants pointed me in the direction of a notorious milk bar just outside the inner city’s Maboneng District.
Pool Seq
And here we finally found our man - playing pool with another character I’ve long been looking for - the Easter bunny. They were playing for flavoured milk shooters, and to get my interview I first had to prove my worth on the table.

Bon: Are you a crook?
Santa: A crook! Do these hands look like they would steal anything? How can you even begin to ask me a question like that?
Bon: But a lot of what you’r doing is breaking and entering. You’re going into people’s homes without their permission.
San: Breaking and entering? I’ve got a contract with the children.
Bongani link in suburb
Now, we’ve spoken to a number of children, and quite surprisingly, many are saying they’re not happy with Santa, because they’re saying he’s not keeping up his end of the bargain

Child 1: I wrote Santa a really nice letter about how i wanted a swimming pool, and he didn’t even get me it.He didn’t even answer the letter.
Child 2: I asked for a PS4, and then on christmas day i look under the tree. i’m super excited, and i look under the tree, and he gets me a pep game.
Child3: It’s not true that Santa Clause doesn’t stealAnd its not true that he doesn't steal. I saw him wearing my dad's shoes.
LINK - Protest outside nursery school. Kids carrying placards stating “Santa must fall” “Pay back the money” etc
Link: With the voices of young people increasingly getting louder, many of them have taken to the streets.
Child: yes, i was good last year but..nothing..
Bongani outside SARS
Our investigation has also revealed that there are concerns with the lack of import duties that Santa is paying for the goods that he brings into the country. And issues about the tax compliance.
Interview with SANTA
Santa: Taxes? How can you even begin to ask me if i pay taxes when I’m importing these things for children?
Bon: Every importer that brings goods, has to pay taxes.
San: For 500 years I’ve done this job and i’ve never had to pay tax yet, and i’m not starting now.
V/o
But SARS begs to differ.
Bongani walking into the SARS office

SARS official: Really i’m breaking a bit of secrecy, because all tax payers have a right to have their own tax affairs protected. But, you know, because of the general interest, i’m going to step out of line with the law and share with you some details about Santa Clauses tax compliance. His compliance with our customs laws, and obviously there is broader compliance concerns with regards to Santa Clause.
Bon: How concerned are you about the goods that Santa Clause is bringing into the country?
Sara: We are concerned. You know he comes in unannounced, he does not come in and declare himself through the various ports of entry. We have a number of ports of entry that people need to come in, if you’re flying into the country, you’ve got to go through a designated port. he just arrives. And he just comes in without any reference to any authority, and, he’s actually been seen to be dumping goods here, and we’re not to sure of their origin.
Bon: Do you have any sense of the scale of his enterprise?
Sars: The trouble is, we’ve been trying to. And we’ve done all that we can to try and find what is he bringing in. We hear reports from across the country of these people who’ve been nice through the year, getting these gifts, and to quantify it is very, very difficult.
Bon: Do you have any other concerns?
Sars: One other thing we are also following on. You know, he drives this sleigh. One of the reindeer, Rudolph, always has a red nose - we are scared that he is consuming alcohol that he is not declaring excise duties on.So we are just following up on that aspect as well because we believe it will obviously contribute to the fiscus in a South African context. The one problem that we have - we haven;t been able to work out which country he resides in, we hear somewhere north, in the cold parts of the world, but we just can’t peg it down. And we haven’t got any tax treaty or anything with that tax authority.

Bon: So why is it so hard for us to track you down?
San: Well, i didn’t know you were looking for me. if you had’ve asked me, if you had’ve looked for me, i would simply have given you a card. if you do want to ask me any questions, please feel free to take that card and call me on my number anytime you want. I welcome you at any stage to look deeper into what I’m doing, and if there’s something wrong, prove it.
Link Bongani outside public protector's office
Until now things have been looking really bad for Santa Clause, but in a surprise twist, the office of the Public Protector has issued a report clearing him of all wrong doing. Titled “Secure in the Comfort of Giving” it says in fact, he’s a good man.
SARS
Sara: Now i’ve just heard i must drop this case. Our senior people have just indicated to me that I must drop this case. But you know, just thinking about it, this guy does a lot of good. And i think in our country today we need more good than bad. We’re not going to follow up on Santa Clause.
Closing link Bongani at a fridge
Well I don't know if there is an age restriction in this contract with Santa. But I'm happy to stock up my fridge and cookie jar... maybe I will get that new car this year...merry Christmas
